title: RC 低通：高音被电容抄了近路
summary: 1.5 kΩ + 100 nF。把频率从低调到高，看输出越来越小；在截止频率和十倍截止频率处测增益和相位。
description: 信号发生器 → R1（1.5 kΩ）→ VOUT → C1（100 nF）→ GND。CH1 看输入，CH2 看 VOUT。用两个通道的幅度比得到增益，认识截止频率 fc = 1/(2πRC) 和伯德图的两条渐近线。

cards.title: 把频率往上拧
text: 信号发生器设成 **正弦波、幅度 `1 V`**，频率从 **`100 Hz`** 开始，慢慢调到 **`10 kHz`**。
频率越来越高时，CH2 的波形变大还是变小？

cards.title: 电容给快信号开了一条近路
text: - 电阻和电容组成一个**分压器**，VOUT 是电容上分到的那一份。
- 电容对慢信号几乎是断开的；信号越快，它越像一根导线，把信号直接引到 GND。所以高频分到的越来越少。
![](fig:divider)
- 电容的“交流电阻”（**容抗**）$X_C = \frac{1}{2π f C}$ 随频率变小。它等于 R 的那个频率叫**截止频率**：
$$f_c = \frac{1}{2π R C}$$
- 在 $f_c$ 处输出是输入的 0.707 倍；过了 $f_c$，频率越高，输出越小。
![](fig:bode)

cards.title: 两个频率，两个通道
text: - 频率调到 **`1061 Hz`**：读 CH2 的 **Vpp**，再读示波器下面的 **CH2 相对 CH1 的相位差**。
- 频率调到 **`10.6 kHz`**：用 CH2 的 Vpp 除以 CH1 的 Vpp，得到幅度比。
- 为什么除以 CH1，而不是除以面板上的 `1 V`：信号发生器里面有 50 Ω，接上电路后端子电压会略低，而且随频率变。两个通道相比，这个误差就抵消了。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **低通**：低于 $f_c$ 几乎原样通过；高于 $f_c$，频率每高 10 倍，输出就小到 1/10，而且越来越落后于输入。
- 工程上把倍数写成**分贝**（dB）：0.707 倍 = −3 dB，1/10 = −20 dB。所以常说“截止频率是 −3 dB 点，之后每十倍频下降 20 dB”。
- $f_c$ 是“输出 = 0.707 × 输入”的频率，只由 R 和 C 决定。
- 坑：瓷片电容常有 ±10%～±20% 的误差，$f_c$ 跟着偏。真实电路里先扫频找 0.707 的那个点，那才是你这块板的 $f_c$。

caption.text: R 和 C 分压：频率越高，C 的容抗 X_C 越小，分到 VOUT 的越少。

i18n.en: R and C divide the input: the higher the frequency, the smaller C's reactance X_C and the smaller VOUT's share.

caption.text: 幅度比随频率变化：f_c 以下几乎是 1，f_c 处是 0.707，再往上越来越小。

i18n.en: Amplitude ratio against frequency: about 1 below f_c, 0.707 at f_c, smaller and smaller above.

en.title: RC low-pass: the capacitor short-cuts the high notes
en.summary: 1.5 kΩ + 100 nF. Turn the frequency up and watch the output shrink; measure gain and phase at the cutoff frequency and ten times it.
en.description: Generator → R1 (1.5 kΩ) → VOUT → C1 (100 nF) → GND. CH1 shows the input, CH2 VOUT. The ratio of the two channels is the gain; meet the cutoff frequency fc = 1/(2πRC) and the two asymptotes of a Bode plot.
compare: - **f = fc/10 = 106 Hz**: |H| = 1/√1.01 ≈ 0.995 (−0.04 dB), phase −5.7°. The signal passes almost unchanged.
- **f = fc = 1061 Hz**: |H| = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707 (−3 dB), phase −45°. That is what "cutoff frequency" means.
- **f = 10fc = 10.6 kHz**: |H| ≈ 1/√101 ≈ 0.0995 (−20 dB), phase −84.3°. Every 10× in frequency divides the amplitude by another 10 (−20 dB/decade), and the phase approaches −90°.

measurements.ask: f = 1061 Hz: the phase of VOUT relative to VIN (negative when CH2 lags)
f = 10.6 kHz (10 fc): the amplitude ratio VOUT/VIN (CH2 Vpp ÷ CH1 Vpp)
measurements.explain: |H| = 1/√(1 + 10²) ≈ 0.0995, i.e. −20 dB: ten times the frequency, about a tenth of the amplitude.

hints: Resistor in series, capacitor from VOUT to GND.
fc = 1/(2πRC). Work out |H| and ∠H at fc first, then compare with the scope.
Compare VOUT with the generator's terminals (CH1), not with the number on the generator's display.
tests: fc/10 = 106 Hz: sensible gain and phase
fc = 1061 Hz: sensible gain and phase

cards.title: Turn the frequency up
text: **Resistor** (`1.5 kΩ`) into **`b3`**–**`b10`**, **capacitor** (`100 nF`) into **`c10`**–**`tn10`**. The probes are already on the board: CH1 on the input, CH2 between the resistor and the capacitor (VOUT).
Set the generator to **sine, amplitude `1 V`**, start at **`100 Hz`** and turn it slowly up to **`10 kHz`**.
As the frequency rises, does the CH2 trace get bigger or smaller?

cards.title: The capacitor is a short-cut for fast signals
text: - The resistor and the capacitor form a **voltage divider**; VOUT is the share that lands on the capacitor.
- A capacitor is almost open for slow signals; the faster the signal, the more it looks like a wire straight to GND. So high frequencies get a smaller and smaller share.
![](fig:divider)
- The capacitor's "AC resistance" (its **capacitive reactance**) $X_C = \frac{1}{2π f C}$ falls with frequency. The frequency where it equals R is the **cutoff frequency**:
$$f_c = \frac{1}{2π R C}$$
- At $f_c$ the output is 0.707 of the input; past $f_c$, the higher the frequency, the smaller the output.
![](fig:bode)

cards.title: Two frequencies, two channels
text: - Set **`1061 Hz`**: read the **Vpp** of CH2, then the **phase of CH2 vs CH1** under the scope screen.
- Set **`10.6 kHz`**: divide CH2's Vpp by CH1's Vpp to get the amplitude ratio.

- Why divide by CH1 and not by the `1 V` on the panel: the generator has 50 Ω inside, so with a circuit attached its terminal voltage is a little lower, and that changes with frequency. Comparing the two channels cancels it.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Low-pass**: below $f_c$ the signal passes almost unchanged; above $f_c$ every 10× in frequency leaves 1/10 of the output, lagging further and further behind the input.
- Engineers write ratios in **decibels** (dB): 0.707 = −3 dB, 1/10 = −20 dB. Hence "the cutoff is the −3 dB point, and above it the gain falls 20 dB per decade".
- $f_c$ is the frequency where output = 0.707 × input. Only R and C set it.
- Pitfall: ceramic capacitors are often ±10% to ±20% off, and $f_c$ moves with them. On a real board, sweep for the 0.707 point first — that is your board's actual $f_c$.

measurements.ask: f = 1061 Hz：VOUT 相对 VIN 的相位差（CH2 滞后为负）
f = 10.6 kHz（10 fc）：幅度比 VOUT/VIN（CH2 的 Vpp ÷ CH1 的 Vpp）

hints: 电阻串联在前，电容从 VOUT 接到 GND。
fc = 1/(2πRC)。先算出 fc 处的 |H| 和 ∠H，再和示波器的读数对比。
拿 VOUT 和信号发生器端子上的电压（CH1）比，而不是和信号发生器面板上的数字比。
